chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq, from Yāsir al-Khādim, who said:

Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام passed by me while I was praying on al-Ṭabarī, and I had placed something upon it on which I would perform sajdah. So he said to me: Why do you not perform sajdah on it? Is it not from the vegetation of the earth?
So the proper way regarding this report is that we carry it upon the state of taqiyyah; that is indicated by this.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: A title for the Imam عليه السلام mentioned in the report
key_terms.أَسْجُدُ: I perform sajdah; the act of prostration in salat (prayer)
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: Taqiyyah; dissimulation or precautionary conformity under specific circumstances
key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: The report or hadith under discussion
key_terms.نَبَاتِ الْأَرْضِ: Vegetation of the earth; a legal criterion mentioned in the report

ai.seo_question: How is the hadith about performing sajdah on cotton or linen understood in al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This report concerns the ruling of performing sajdah on a material identified as being from the vegetation of the earth. The compiler then clarifies that the report is to be understood in the context of taqiyyah, indicating its legal significance in reconciling narrations on the subject of سجود.
